title: Tata Trusts rift deepens: Noel Tata-led trustees say 'Trusts do not run Tata Sons' as they defend restructuring plan to avoid listing
excerpt: Trustees of Tata Trusts have rebuffed objections from two senior trustees concerning a proposed restructuring of Tata Sons. They emphasized that the Reserve Bank of India has not required a listing for Tata Sons. Additionally, they asserted that the restructuring does not jeopardize the charitable status of the trusts. The trustees referenced past resolutions in support of preserving Tata Sons' unlisted status.

title: U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, August 2026
excerpt: The U.S. goods and services trade deficit increased in August 2026 according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and the U.S. Census Bureau. The deficit increased from $92.8 billion in July (revised) to $105.6 billion in August, as imports increased more than exports. The goods deficit increased $12.8 billion in August to $136.6 billion. The services surplus increased less than $0.1 billion in August to $31.0 billion.

title: Tata Sons mulling legal view on Trusts offer, not seen as a Trusts resolution to be considered
excerpt: Tata Sons board has not yet formally met to consider the restructuring proposal from Tata Trusts. Tata Trusts, as majority shareholders, suggested the restructuring to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.
